'''Kam-Biu Luk''' ({{lang-zh|t=陸錦標}}, born 1953) is a professor of physics, with a focus on particle physics, at [[UC Berkeley]] and a senior faculty scientist in the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]'s physics division.<ref name=LBNLPanofsky>{{cite web|title=Berkeley's Kam-Biu Luk Wins Panofsky Prize for Daya Bay Experiment|url=http://newscenter.lbl.gov/science-shorts/2013/09/30/berkeleys-kam-biu-luk-wins-panofsky-prize-for-daya-bay-experiment/|publisher=Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|access-date=2013-10-06|date=2013-09-30}}</ref> Luk has conducted research on [[neutrino oscillation]] and [[CP violation]]. Luk and his collaborator [[Wang Yifang|Yifang Wang]] were awarded the 2014 [[Panofsky Prize]] "for their leadership of the [[Daya Bay Reactor Neutrino Experiment|Daya Bay experiment]], which produced the first definitive measurement of θ<sub>13</sub> angle of the neutrino mixing matrix."<ref name=LBNLPanofsky/><ref name=2014PanofskyPrize>{{cite web|title=2014 W.K.H. Panofsky Prize in Experimental Particle Physics Recipient|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Luk&first_nm=Kam-Biu&year=2014|publisher=American Physical Society|access-date=2013-10-06}}</ref> His work on neutrino oscillation also received 2016 Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics shared with other teams.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://breakthroughprize.org/News/29|title=Breakthrough Prize|website=breakthroughprize.org|access-date=2016-06-16}}</ref>
He also received a Doctor of Science honoris causa from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology in 2016. Luk is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]],<ref name=LBNLPanofsky/> and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].

==Education and career==
Luk graduated from [[Ying Wa College]] in 1973, then graduated from the [[University of Hong Kong]] in 1976 with a [[Bachelor of Science|B.Sc]] in physics.<ref name=Facultypage>{{cite web|title=Kam-Biu Luk|url=http://physics.berkeley.edu/index.php?option=com_dept_management&act=people&Itemid=312&limitstart=0&task=view&id=365|publisher=Physics Department UC Berkeley|access-date=2013-10-06}}</ref> Shortly thereafter, Luk joined [[Rutgers University]]'s physics Ph.D. program, completing his Ph.D. in 1983.

Luk continued his work in physics by conducting his postdoctoral research at the [[University of Washington in Seattle]] until 1986. In 1986, Luk became an R.R. Wilson Fellow at [[Fermilab]], where he worked as an associate scientist until 1989. In 1989, Luk received a joint appointment as an assistant professor of the Physics Department at [[UC Berkeley]] and faculty scientist at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]. During his first two years working in Berkeley, Luk received the "Department of Energy outstanding junior investigator award", which is designed to "identify exceptionally talented new high energy physicists early in their careers, and to assist and facilitate the development of their research programs".<ref name=Facultypage/><ref name=DOEJIAward>{{cite web|title=OUTSTANDING JUNIOR INVESTIGATOR PROGRAM|url=http://www.er.doe.gov/hep/hep_grants/oji_program.shtml|publisher=US Department of Energy|access-date=2013-10-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130819082725/http://www.er.doe.gov/hep/hep_grants/oji_program.shtml|archive-date=2013-08-19|url-status=dead}}</ref> Luk was awarded a [[Sloan Fellowship]] between 1990 and 1994, which is awarded to "those who show the most outstanding promise of making fundamental contributions to new knowledge".<ref name=Facultypage/><ref name=SFA>{{cite web|title=History of the Sloan Fellowship|url=http://www.sloan.org/sloan-research-fellowships/history/|publisher=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation|access-date=2013-10-06|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120908235159/http://www.sloan.org/sloan-research-fellowships/history/|archive-date=2012-09-08}}</ref>

Luk became a Miller Professor at UC Berkeley in the fall of 2001.<ref name=Facultypage/> He was also a visiting professor in [[Hong Kong University of Science and Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|title=visiting professor HKUST|url=http://web.phys.ust.hk/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=345&Itemid=128|access-date=2016-06-16|archive-date=2016-10-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161007222202/http://web.phys.ust.hk/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=345&Itemid=128|url-status=dead}}</ref> Luk is currently a Hung Hing Ying distinguished visiting professor in science of
The University of Hong Kong, and a senior visiting fellow of the Jockey Club Institute for Advanced Study at the Hong Kong University of Science and
Technology.

==Research area==
Luk conducts research in [[particle physics]] both as a professor at [[UC Berkeley]] and as a scientist at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]. Luk has published a number of papers on [[neutrino oscillation]] (see selected publications), including his 2014 [[Panofsky Prize]] winning research at the [[Daya Bay Nuclear Power Plant]].<ref name=LBNLPanofsky/><ref name=Neutrinoexperiment>{{cite web|title=Daya Bay Reactor Neutrino Experiment|url=http://neutrino.physics.berkeley.edu/|publisher=UC Berkeley and LBNL|access-date=2013-10-07}}</ref>  Luk is also known for his work on hyperon physics. His Ph.D. dissertation laid the foundation for determining the polarization of the {{Math|Ω<sup>−</sup>}} [[Omega baryon|hyperon]]. Along with a
small group of young colleagues, he initiated Fermilab E756 to measure the magnetic dipole moment of the Omega-minus hyperon. He discovered polarization of the charged anti-cascade hyperon that laid the experimental foundation for investigating CP violation in charged-cascade decays. In the 1990s, Luk proposed the HyperCP (E871) project conducted at [[Fermilab]], where he and a team of scientists conducted an experiment "designed to search for direct CP Violation in strange-baryon decays with the best precision in the world.".<ref name=fermilab>{{cite web|title=CP Violation in Hyperon Decays|url=http://ppd.fnal.gov/experiments/e871/|publisher=Fermilab|access-date=2013-10-07}}</ref><ref name=research>{{cite journal|last=Luk|first=Kam-Biu|author2=T. Holmstrom|title=Search for CP Violation in Charged-Ξ and Λ Hyperon Decays|journal=Physical Review Letters|date=21 December 2004|volume=93|issue=14|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.65.1713|pmid=10042344|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.93.262001|display-authors=etal|pages=1713–1716|bibcode=2004PhRvL9326L2001H|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He continues to explore CP Violation but in the neutrino sector through the participation of DUNE.
